item.title: Trump’s DHS Asks Supreme Court to Allow Border Wall in Big Bend
item.description: President Donald Trump’s administration asked the US Supreme Court to let border-wall construction resume in Big Bend National Park in west Texas, setting up a high-stakes clash over one of his longstanding priorities.
item.dc:creator: Greg Stohr

item.title: How China’s Government Works: Guide to Xi Jinping’s Power Structure
item.description: China is governed through a labyrinth of committees, conferences and other bodies. Here's a guide to understanding its complicated political universe.
item.dc:creator: Josh Xiao

item.title: JD Vance’s 2028 Ambitions Face an Early Test in Midterms
item.description: The vice president’s unpopularity and actions on the stump may prove to be a challenge for a 2028 bid.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan

item.title: Richard Branson Says Venezuela Needs Elections to Draw Investment
item.description: Billionaire Richard Branson, a prominent critic of the ousted Nicolás Maduro, said Venezuela must hold elections and establish rule of law to secure more foreign investment.
item.dc:creator: Andreina Itriago

item.title: Meta Offers Zuckerberg New Shares to Shield Him From Wealth Tax
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. signed an agreement with Mark Zuckerberg to keep him living in the same jurisdiction as the company’s headquarters after the CEO said he was weighing leaving California if the state passes a wealth tax.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Paulden

item.title: Small Business Resilience Boosting Growth
item.description: Small businesses remain a driving force behind economic growth, job creation, and opportunity across the country. Bloomberg Businessweek Daily is Live from the Chase for Business Make Your Move Summit, highlighting the resilience and impact of small businesses across the country. Chase for Business CEO Stevie Baron says while most small business owners are optimistic about their own outlook, that sentiment does not match how they feel about the overall economy. We also hear from Chase for Business Executive Director Dan Russell on how small businesses are boosting the sunbelt economy. Plus Katie Kirkpatrick, President & CEO of the Metro Atlanta Chamber, and Diedra Porché, National Head of Community and Business Development at JPMorganChase, discuss how investments in small businesses boost local economies. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Waives Red Diesel Tax Record Requirements to Entice Buyers
item.description: The Trump administration is waiving recordkeeping requirements in a bid to encourage farmers, truck-stop operators and other companies to buy tax-exempt red diesel.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Elon Musk’s Texas Senate Race Donations Play Into James Talarico’s Hand
item.description: Elon Musk’s move to spend millions of dollars to support Republican Ken Paxton in his US Senate race is opening up a potent line of attack about money in politics from Democratic challenger James Talarico.
item.dc:creator: Dana Hull, Bill Allison and Joe Lovinger

item.title: Putin Says Russia Ready for Talks
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the White House. On today's show, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, American Principles Project Political Director Katie Frost, Kuwait Petroleum Corporation CEO Sheikh Nawaf Al-Sabah and Sabato's Crystal Ball Managing Editor Kyle Kondik. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Carney Announces $6.4 Billion Plan for Ontario Steel and Autos
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney unveiled a C$9 billion ($6.4 billion) partnership with Ontario to support the province’s tariff-battered steel and auto industries, along with new funding for mining-related infrastructure in the Ring of Fire region.
item.dc:creator: Brian Platt

item.title: Trump May Turn Briefing Room Into a Pool: NY Times
item.description: President Donald Trump has talked about replacing the White House press briefing room with an indoor swimming pool. This is according to the New York Times. The outlet says he's been considering the move since August. Trump has been at odds with some in the press over what he calls unfair coverage. Bloomberg's Catherine Lucey reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sabato's Crystal Ball Moves 28 House Races Toward Dems
item.description: Kyle Kondik, managing editor of Sabato’s Crystal Ball at University of Virginia’s Center for Politics, said that the upcoming midterm elections will be about 'overall environment' than about developments in individual races. Sabato's Crystal Ball moved 28 House ratings toward Democrats earlier this week and Kondik said that Democrats will do 'quite well' in swing House districts, while control of the Senate is still 'up in the air.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Musk Says SpaceX, Tesla Merger Makes Sense
item.description: Elon Musk says combining SpaceX and Tesla makes sense. "There’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software," he said during the SpaceX earnings webcast on Tuesday. Musk, who is chief executive officer of both companies, says he won't take part in any committee discussions about the idea. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ramaswamy Faces Blowback on Ad With Rival’s Estranged Mother
item.description: Republican biotech entrepreneur and former presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy is facing bipartisan backlash over a $4 million advertisement he supported against his opponent in the campaign to be Ohio’s next governor.
item.dc:creator: Miranda Davis, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Mark Niquette

item.title: Putin Releases Hostage to US, Earning Praise as Humanitarian
item.description: The Trump administration praised Russian President Vladimir Putin as a “humanitarian” for releasing a detained US citizen, the latest White House move to curry favor with Russia in its efforts to end the war in Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Iain Marlow

item.title: UN Suggests Meta ‘Disproportionately’ Curbed Lula Posts
item.description: United Nations experts said Meta Platforms Inc. “disproportionately curtailed” accounts linked to one side of Brazil’s presidential race, in an apparent reference to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s campaign.
item.dc:creator: Augusta Saraiva

item.title: US Asks Federal Court to Reconsider Another Wind Farm Approval
item.description: The Trump administration wants to reconsider an approval for a wind farm proposed off the Massachusetts coast by Avangrid Inc., threatening to stoke more uncertainty for a deal to reform the US system of permitting big energy projects.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter

item.title: Quebec Separatist Government Picks Marceau as Finance Minister
item.description: The newly elected separatist government in Quebec appointed economist Nicolas Marceau as its finance minister on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Dion

item.title: Georgia GOP Candidate Jackson Loans $20 Million to Trump-Touted Oil Refinery
item.description: Georgia GOP gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson loaned $20 million at 12% interest to a new oil refinery planned for the Texas coast that President Donald Trump has hailed as a major victory in his quest for “energy dominance.”
item.dc:creator: Nathan Risser

item.title: US-Mexico Trade Talks Hit Impasse as Lutnick Weighs In
item.description: US and Mexican trade negotiators have hit an impasse over tariffs on steel and aluminum, dashing earlier optimism for an imminent deal and likely kicking major progress until after the midterm elections, people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Diaz, Eric Martin and Gonzalo Soto
